About Our Client
Wellness Equity Alliance is a national multidisciplinary health organization focused on addressing health inequities through integrated, community-based care. The organization delivers medical care, behavioral health services, substance use treatment, harm reduction, and care coordination through mobile and field-based models in settings such as schools, rural communities, reentry sites, and community-based locations.
About the Opportunity
The Patient Care Coordinator
conducts telephonic outreach to prospective CalAIM members, connecting eligible individuals with Enhanced Care Management (ECM) and Community Supports programs. This fully remote position focuses on patient engagement, program education, eligibility screening, and enrollment coordination while supporting improved access to community-based care.
Responsibilities
• Conduct high-volume outbound calls to prospective members from referrals and lead lists.
• Explain Enhanced Care Management, Community Supports, and other available services.
• Build rapport with individuals, including those who may be hesitant to participate.
• Screen individuals for program eligibility and interest.
• Schedule enrollment appointments and coordinate warm handoffs to Care Managers and clinical team members.
• Accurately document outreach activities, patient interactions, and enrollment outcomes.
• Meet productivity expectations related to outreach volume, contact rates, and enrollment goals.
• Follow established workflows, scripts, and compliance requirements.
• Collaborate with supervisors and program staff to improve outreach effectiveness.
• Maintain confidentiality and comply with HIPAA and privacy requirements.
• Participate in team meetings, training, and quality improvement initiatives.
• Complete required follow-up activities within established timelines.
• Perform other duties as assigned.
Requirements
• High school diploma or equivalent.
• Minimum 1 year of experience in patient-centered care, healthcare outreach, call center operations, care coordination, or a related field.
• Excellent verbal communication and active listening skills.
• Strong organizational and documentation skills.
• Ability to manage a high volume of outbound calls with professionalism and empathy.
• Proficiency with Microsoft Office and web-based applications.
• Ability to work independently in a remote environment.
• Strong interpersonal skills and cultural sensitivity.
• Commitment to advancing health equity and improving access to care.
• Knowledge of HIPAA and related privacy and documentation standards.
Preferred Qualifications
• Experience working with Medicaid/Medi-Cal populations.
• Experience with CalAIM programs.

jobs.description:
Overview

Alnylam (Nasdaq: ALNY) is delivering on a bold vision to turn scientific possibility into reality, with a robust RNA interference (RNAi) therapeutics platform. As the pioneer in RNAi and the leading RNAi therapeutics company, we have always been uncompromisingly dedicated to translating the breakthrough science into transformational medicines to help as many people as possible. Long focused on rare and genetic diseases, our scientific advances are now allowing us to bring the power of RNAi therapeutics to more prevalent diseases and as a result, we are beginning to recognize the full potential of this new class of medicines.

Alnylam is committed to its journey to become a top 5 independent, global biopharma company. We are already admired and recognized for our dedication to patients, company culture that empowers people to do their best work, track record of scientific innovation, social responsibility, and commercial excellence.

Founded in 2002, and headquartered in Cambridge, Mass., Alnylam has over 1,650 employees at work across the globe. We are seeking smart, passionate, “change the world” kind of people who are ready to say, “challenge accepted” to our mission. Thanks to the commitment of every employee globally, Alnylam is proud to have been recognized as one of Fast Company’s 2021 Best Workplaces for Innovators, a Science Magazine Top Employer three years in a row (2019-2021), a Boston Globe Top Places to Work seven years in a row (2015-2021), a Great Place to Work in Asia, Japan, Brazil, the U.K., Germany, Spain, Netherlands, Italy, France and Switzerland, Seramount’s 100 Best Companies (formerly Working Mother 100 Best Companies) and Best Companies for Dads, Bloomberg’s Gender Equality Index two years in a row (2021-2022), among others. At Alnylam, we are committed to fostering a diverse, equitable and inclusive work environment, culture, and workforce, and we support several Employee Resource Networks.

Summary Of Key Responsibilities

Assess patients’ needs and develop action plans that provide for the initiation and continuation of treatment with Alnylam products while coordinating the exchange of all applicable patient-related information with appropriate internal and external stakeholders.
Develops a comprehensive understanding of the reimbursement process, billing/coding nuances, insurance plans, payer trends, financial assistance programs, patient assistance programs, and related resources.

Understands the resources available in their specific region, and how they can be best employed to support patient care.
Identifies complex patient-specific issues and develops and executes action plans accordingly.
Maintains disease, reimbursement and insurance coverage expertise through continuing medical education and attendance at relevant conferences and other educational opportunities.
Educates patients, caregivers, family members, health care providers, and others regarding insurance options and limitations, including PA and policy requirements necessary to initiate and maintain treatment, patient services’ offerings and relevant disease/product information as necessary.
Fosters collaborative relationships with all internal and external customers including but not limited to Patient Education Liaisons, medical, sales, field reimbursement, corporate accounts, patient advocacy, insurance company case managers, specialty pharmacies, home health agencies, and office coordinators.

Ensures compliance with all corporate and industry policies in collaboration with Alnylam Legal, Regulatory and Compliance.

Bachelor’s Degree required. Health Care/Social Work/Nursing (or related field) a plus.
3+ years recent case management experience in the healthcare or pharmaceutical/biotech industry. Ultra-rare disease experience a plus.
Experience should include but not be limited to home care management, case management review, utilization review, social service support, insurance reimbursement, patient assistance programs, or billing and coding.
Knowledge of benefit verification and prior authorization process for infused and injectable products.
Knowledge of private payer, Medicare, and Medicaid structure, systems, and reimbursement process required.
Experience and proficiency in working with a Customer Relationship Management System, such as Salesforce.com.
Possess strong written and verbal communication skills, exceptional listening, critical thinking, problem solving, negotiation and mediation skills.
Ability to navigate difficult conversations and handle sensitive issues with opposing opinions.
Ability to work independently and manage competing priorities.
Experience working in cross-functional teams and effective in influencing without authority.
Desire to innovate and work in a fast-paced, flexible, and energetic environment.
Self-starter who is highly passionate about rare disease and Alnylam’s core values:
Commitment to People, Innovation and Discovery, Sense of Urgency, Open Culture, and Passion for Excellence.

Ability to travel 5%, including weekends/evenings, as needed.

U.S. Pay Range

$85,500.00 - $115,600.00

Base pay will be determined based on a number of factors including, but not limited to, relevant experience, skills, and education. This role is eligible for an annual short-term incentive award (e.g., bonus or sales incentive) and an annual long-term incentive award (e.g., equity).

We offer comprehensive benefits including medical, dental, and vision coverage, life and disability insurance, a lifestyle reimbursement program, flexible spending and health savings accounts and a 401(k)with a generous company match. Eligible employees enjoy paid time off, wellness days, holidays, and two company-wide recharge breaks. We also offer generous family resources and leave. Our commitment to your well-being reflects our belief that caring for our people fuels the impact we create together.

Learn more about these and additional benefits offered by Alnylam by visiting the Benefits section of the Careers website: https://www.alnylam.com/careers

We are the leader in RNAi therapeutics – a revolutionary approach with the potential to transform the lives of people with rare and common diseases. Built on Nobel Prize-winning science, Alnylam has delivered the breakthroughs that made RNAi therapeutics possible and are just at the beginning of what’s possible. Our deep pipeline, late-stage programs, and bold vision reflect our core values: fierce innovation, passion for excellence, purposeful urgency, open culture and commitment to people. jobs.title: Patient Care Coordinator/Medical Assistant
jobs.description:
Zarminali Pediatrics is building the nation's leading pediatric multispecialty group, focused on supporting families to shape healthy futures for their children – from birth through adulthood – by completely transforming the way pediatric care is delivered nationwide. We are tackling today's challenges of increased administrative burden on clinicians and a siloed approach to pediatric care through intentional design of care delivery, enhanced by leading technology and collaborative, expert care teams.

Our name, inspired by our founder's daughter's name – Zarmina – means “something that is more precious to you than gold”. We couldn’t think of anything that better represents the way parents and caregivers hold the relationship with their children as the most valuable gift, and how we at Zarminali approach care for each child with equal reverence.

We strive for a healthier future for pediatric patients and a happier future for pediatric clinicians nationwide, and we are looking for people to join us in achieving this vision. If you are eager to join a growth stage company and be part of the early team that is shaping the foundation of both the company and the delivery of pediatric care, then this opportunity might be for you!

As a Patient Care Coordinator / Medical Assistant (PCC/MA)
in Denver, Colorado, you will play a vital dual role in delivering an exceptional patient experience while providing high-quality clinical support. This cross-trained position combines front office responsibilities with Medical Assistant duties to ensure seamless clinic operations and an outstanding experience for every child and family we serve.

You will serve as a trusted partner to patients, families, providers, and teammates—supporting the patient journey from scheduling and check-in through discharge and follow-up. This role requires flexibility, adaptability, and a team-first mindset, as responsibilities will shift between front office and clinical support based on daily operational needs.

WHAT YOU’LL DO:

Patient Experience & Front Office

Welcome patients and families with a warm, friendly, and professional demeanor.
Manage patient check-in and check-out processes while delivering exceptional customer service.
Collect, verify, and update demographic, insurance, and registration information within the EMR.
Schedule appointments, follow-up visits, referrals, and diagnostic services.
Answer incoming phone calls, respond to patient inquiries, and direct calls appropriately.
Collect copays and process patient payments in accordance with company policies.
Support patient communication through phone calls, portal messages, appointment reminders, and follow-up outreach.
Assist with referral coordination, prior authorizations, and medical records requests.
Maintain accurate patient records while ensuring HIPAA compliance.
Support opening and closing clinic procedures and maintain an organized, welcoming front office.

Clinical Care & Provider Support

Greet, room, and prepare patients for appointments.
Complete patient intake, obtain vital signs, and document information accurately in the EMR.
Perform point-of-care testing (strep, flu, RSV, COVID, hemoglobin, etc.).
Administer vaccines safely and accurately while monitoring for adverse reactions.
Assist physicians and advanced practice providers during patient visits and procedures.
Prepare and stock exam rooms while maintaining infection prevention and control standards.
Support medication refills, referrals, patient recalls, and other clinical follow-up activities.
Ensure accurate and timely clinical documentation.

Team Collaboration & Clinic Operations

Rotate between front office and clinical responsibilities based on daily staffing and patient volume.
Provide cross-coverage to ensure efficient clinic operations and an exceptional patient experience.
Collaborate closely with providers and teammates to improve workflows and patient satisfaction.
Contribute to continuous process improvement and operational excellence.
Serve as a positive ambassador for the clinic's mission, vision, and values.

WHAT YOU’LL NEED:

High school diploma or equivalent.
Current Certified Medical Assistant (CMA) is preferred.
BLS certification required
1+ year of experience in a medical assistant or patient-facing healthcare role.
Comfort navigating electronic medical records and scheduling systems.
Strong interpersonal and communication skills.
Ability to multitask and remain organized in a fast-paced environment.
A collaborative mindset and willingness to be cross-trained.
Commitment to delivering compassionate, inclusive, and family-centered care.

WHAT WE OFFER:

A collaborative, team-based environment focused on high-quality pediatric care.
Cross-training and skill development that expands your professional growth.
Opportunities to grow within a fast-scaling, mission-driven organization.
The opportunity to help build something meaningful within your community.

At Zarminali Pediatrics, we are committed to our empowering clinicians and team members to deliver better pediatric care, altogether. This commitment requires building an inclusive culture and a team that represents the diverse communities we serve.

We believe that when people from all backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives come together, we create a stronger team and better care for our patients and their families. We realize the importance of an environment where clinicians and team members feel cared for, supported, and valued. We believe in the basics: treating everyone with kindness, respect, and fairness.

We do not tolerate discrimination or harassment of any kind. This includes, but is not limited to, race, color, sex, gender, age, religion or religious creed, national origin, ancestry, citizenship, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, genetic information, physical or mental disability, military or veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

We recruit and hire based on skills, talent, and potential, ensuring everyone has a fair chance to succeed. Together, we strive to build an inclusive and welcoming space where we can achieve our goal of building a happier future for the pediatric workforce.

jobs.description:

At Regional Transportation District (RTD), We make lives better through connections!

When you join RTD, you will be among dedicated employees exhibiting RTD's values of passion, respect, diversity, trustworthiness, collaboration, and ownership. RTD is committed to an inclusive and diverse workplace. As part of our diversity value statement, we encourage our employees to honor diversity in thought, people, and experience. Come join RTD on this great journey to be the trusted leader in mobility, delivering excellence and value to our customers and community.

RTD Employee Benefits: https://www.rtd-denver.com/careers/benefits

(RTD Represented Employee Benefits: Please refer to the Labor Agreement included in the above link for details.)

This position provides operational leadership and direct supervisory oversight for RTD’s bus fleet, including diesel, gas, hybrid, and battery-electric/zero-emission revenue and non-revenue vehicles. This position is responsible for overseeing vehicle and equipment maintenance activities, supporting safe, reliable, and cost-effective fleet operations, and providing daily supervision, guidance, and direction to maintenance personnel.

The role coordinates and supervises the work of assigned staff performing bus vehicle maintenance and repair functions, including managing shift assignments, conducting performance evaluations, providing coaching and corrective guidance, and resolving routine and moderately complex operational issues. The Supervisor serves as a key operational leader within the department, ensuring adherence to labor agreements, internal policies, safety standards, and applicable federal, state, and local regulations. This includes reviewing maintenance reports, monitoring performance data, supporting maintenance scheduling, and implementing corrective actions to maintain fleet reliability and safety.

This position monitors departmental resources and supports budget and operational controls by tracking expenditures, managing overtime within established guidelines, and promoting efficient maintenance practices. The Supervisor oversees maintenance campaigns, coordinates repair and modification programs, supports parts procurement and staging, and ensures maintenance activities comply with established procedures and documentation standards.

The Supervisor collects, analyzes, and reports operational and performance data, monitoring key performance indicators (KPIs) to evaluate fleet effectiveness, identify trends, and implement improvements that enhance maintenance efficiency and cost control. The position remains informed on industry best practices, evolving vehicle technologies, and regulatory requirements to support continuous improvement in fleet maintenance and reliability.

This position collaborates with internal departments, external partners, and vendors to resolve maintenance challenges, coordinate fleet initiatives, and ensure the availability and readiness of vehicles for service. Success in this role requires strong supervisory leadership, sound technical knowledge of bus maintenance practices, and the ability to guide maintenance teams in a dynamic environment while ensuring fleet safety, compliance, and operational performance.

Essential

DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES:

Participate in the hiring, onboarding, and personnel actions involving direct reports. Provide ongoing supervision of work unit performance, including assigning work, setting expectations, and ensuring staff have the tools, training, and resources needed to perform effectively. Take or recommend corrective and disciplinary action as appropriate. Promote professional development, accountability, and equitable treatment across the workforce.
Plan, direct, and coordinate RTD’s rolling stock maintenance function, including maintenance and repair of bus fleets (diesel, gas, hybrid, and battery electric/zero-emission revenue and non-revenue vehicles). Ensure vehicle readiness, safety, reliability, and performance meet operational standards and service requirements.
Serve as the primary supervisory authority for staff performing bus vehicle and equipment maintenance.Assign and delegate shift work, monitor productivity and work quality, and ensure effective execution of all maintenance activities across assigned areas.
Oversee vehicle and equipment maintenance programs, including preventive and corrective maintenance,repair campaigns, and staging of critical resources (parts, tools, and equipment). Direct troubleshooting efforts and ensure timely resolution of mechanical and system issues.
Develop, implement, and maintain departmental policies, procedures, and maintenance documentation,ensuring accurate records of inspections, repairs, safety compliance, and maintenance activities.
Develop, monitor, and manage the departmental budget, including oversight of expenditures, overtime control, staffing levels, and cost-effective resource allocation in alignment with service demands and operational priorities.
Administer labor agreements and resolve workplace issues in coordination with management, ensuring consistent application of contract provisions and department policies.
Support the development of vehicle specifications for new bus procurements, including revenue and non-revenue vehicles and support equipment, ensuring maintainability, safety, and operational performance requirements are incorporated.
Collect, validate, analyze, and report maintenance performance metrics and operational data. Use data to evaluate fleet reliability, vehicle availability, safety performance, and cost efficiency, and implement corrective or improvement actions as needed.
Collaborate with internal departments including Operations, Safety, Service Planning, Finance, and Procurement to resolve maintenance issues, improve vehicle availability, and ensure alignment with agency operational goals.
Lead committees, task forces, and working groups related to fleet maintenance, vehicle safety, performance improvement, and operational efficiency, ensuring accountability for outcomes and follow-through on recommendations.
Direct investigation, response, and resolution of vehicle or equipment failures and maintenance-related service disruptions, ensuring timely corrective action and minimizing operational impact.
Represent RTD at industry, inter agency, and stakeholder meetings related to fleet maintenance and vehicle operations, ensuring consistent communication, transparency, and accountability.
Support implementation of strategic initiatives aligned with RTD priorities, including safety, reliability,financial stewardship, and system sustainability.
Lead special projects and operational initiatives, including risk assessments related to fleet maintenance,ensuring successful execution and alignment with operational objectives.
Direct training, outreach activities, and forums for maintenance staff and stakeholders to support skill development, safety awareness, and operational consistency.
Prepare and review technical analyses, reports, and presentations for internal leadership, external stakeholders, and governing bodies related to fleet maintenance operations.
Establish and maintain strong working relationships across departments and promote cross-functional collaboration to ensure safe, reliable, and efficient bus maintenance operations.
This position is designated as a Disaster Response Worker, which may require night and weekend work during natural disasters and other emergencies (e.g., activation of 24-hour Emergency Operations Center staffing). Regular office hours and work schedules may vary and include weekdays, weekends, and hours outside of 7:45 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.
Becoming a maintenance technician is one of the best ways for management employees to gain first hand experience of RTD's transit operations. You may be required to obtain or maintain certification/qualification as a maintenance technician.
The position may be required to work in any of the following bus, commuter, light rail, and paratransit functions within operations and maintenance depending on business needs and/or career growth and development: Regional Operations Center, Operations, Maintenance, and Service Planning & Scheduling.

Other

All job-related duties as assigned.

Qualifications

High school diploma or equivalent required. Technical or vocational training in diesel technology, automotive technology, heavy equipment maintenance, electrical systems, or a related field is desirable.
Minimum of three (3) years of progressively responsible experience in bus, heavy vehicle, or fleet maintenance operations. Experience must include working directly with maintenance staff, coordinating repair activities, and supporting safe and reliable vehicle operations.
Experience supporting or performing inspection, maintenance, and repair of transit bus fleets, including diesel, gas, hybrid, and battery-electric/zero-emission vehicles. Experience should include preventive maintenance, troubleshooting mechanical and electrical systems, diagnosing vehicle faults, coordinating repairs, and ensuring vehicles meet operational readiness standards.
Knowledge of applicable local, state, and federal safety and operational standards governing transit fleet maintenance, including FTA, APTA, OSHA, environmental, and workplace safety regulations as they relate to heavy vehicle maintenance and shop operations.
Ability to supervise, train, and provide guidance to maintenance personnel, including assigning work, monitoring performance, and ensuring compliance with safety procedures, maintenance standards, and departmental policies in a dynamic transit maintenance environment.
Must have a valid Colorado driver's license or the ability to obtain one within 90 days of hire. No DUI, DWI, or Reckless Driving violations in the past 5 years.

POSITION OVERVIEW:

The Clinical Supervisor is responsible for all clinical aspects of treatment for the patients they oversee. This includes the assessment and analysis of the patient’s skills and challenging behaviors, development of treatment plans, overseeing the implementation of treatment, collaboration with and training of their patient’s caregivers, as well as ongoing coaching and training of behavioral technicians. • Analyze challenging behaviors to identify the function of the behavior
• Develop functionally relevant treatment plans to reduce challenging behaviors
• Observe treatment implementation for potential program revisions
• Monitor treatment integrity to ensure satisfactory implementation of treatment protocols
• Direct behavior technicians in the implementation of new or revised treatment protocols
• Provides ongoing coaching and training to behavioral technicians
• Primarily works physically within the center to support technicians and follow best practices of direct observation
• Summarize and analyze data to evaluate patient progress towards treatment goals and adjust treatment protocols based upon data
• Update treatment plans at least once per month, based upon patient response to treatment
• Fulfill a minimum of 120 payor/client authorized billable hours per month, inclusive of Supervisory hours and therapy hours
• Accurately communicate treatment response to treatment stakeholders (i.e., caregivers, payers)
• Coordinate care with other professionals
• Administer, complete, and score standardized assessments
• Includes caregiver as a part of the treatment team, as evidenced by consistent Caregiver Collaboration meetings
• Interacts with payers in a way that is collaborative, professional, thorough, and informative
• Engages with payers as needed for funding meetings (i.e., IEP, peer reviews)
• Stay up to date on best practices for ABA treatment to ensure clinical excellence
• Maintains appropriate documentation in Skills and the patient’s medical record
• Communicate effectively and compassionately with patients, families and colleagues
• Provide a safe and supportive environment for patients, families and colleagues
• Maintain compliance with HIPAA requirements at all times
• Partner consistently and effectively with other center leadership including but not limited to: Operations Manager, Clinical Supervisors, Administrative Coordinator Technician, Behavior Technician Leads
• Other duties as assigned

REQUIREMENTS:

• Certification as a behavior analyst from the Behavior Analyst Certification Board required
• Experience working with individuals with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) required

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES:

• Empathetic and compassionate individual with the ability to maintain strict confidentiality
• Ability to work collaboratively with team members while maintaining a positive and solution focused attitude
• Ability to work independently to problem solve and exercise clinical judgment
• An effective communicator in both verbal and written formats
• Demonstrate excellent time management skills and the ability to work in a fast paced, changing environment
• Excellent computer skills and knowledge of MS Excel, Word, Outlook; ability to use new computer systems and iPads.
• Desire to continuously learn and develop skillsets
• Willingness to work in a variety of locations (center, patient home, etc.)
• Willingness to work with a variety of patients
• Reliable means of transportation with proof of auto insurance
• Must pass tuberculosis test
• Proficiency in English, both written and verbal

WORK ENVIRONMENT:

Treatment may occur in a variety of settings including the patient’s home, the CARD center, the patient’s school, the community, or via telehealth. Clinical Supervisors work in environments that are both indoors and outdoors and may move between different locations throughout the course of the workday. Treatment environments may be subject to loud or excessive noise at times.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS:

• Be able to work with patients who are seated on the floor, in small chairs, or other home, school, community and clinic environments
• Move frequently throughout the therapeutic setting to gather materials, anticipate and respond to the movement of a patient, and/or provide instruction in a variety of settings, such as school, playground, clinic, or community locations
• Constantly position oneself to participate and respond to the movements and behaviors of patients, including but not limited to bending to assist a patient, kneeling/crouching to teach a play skill, hurrying to block an open doorway, or reaching to prevent a patient from entering a traffic congested street

r helps families strengthen their functioning, increase self-sufficiency, and prepare for successful independent living at program exit.

$120,000/year W2 salary paid weekly, with medical, dental, and vision benefits starting on day one
On-site position at an Alpha campus in Malibu, CA; San Francisco, CA; Santa Barbara, CA; Boston, MA; New York City, NY; or Miami Beach, FL (relocation assistance available).

Traditional schools set expectations. You'll guide students to surpass what they think is possible.

Every young person holds potential they haven't yet recognized. When students face difficulty, most adults reduce demands. Your approach is different. You understand that confidence doesn't emerge from empty praise—it grows when someone accomplishes what they previously considered beyond reach. If you've refused to allow a student, athlete, camper, or mentee to give up on themselves, this work will resonate with you.

Alpha has redesigned education around one core principle: AI excels at academic delivery, while exceptional people excel at transforming lives. Students handle core academics through adaptive, AI-driven learning platforms. Your responsibility is cultivating what technology cannot—discipline, resilience, communication, ownership, focus, and the conviction that challenging pursuits are worthwhile. Your day won't involve delivering lectures or grading assignments. Instead, you'll coach students through obstacles, recognize meaningful progress, and support them in reaching goals they previously deemed impossible.

Approximately 60% of your time goes toward facilitating energetic, one-hour life skills workshops covering subjects like public speaking, focus, leadership, and feedback exchange. Roughly 30% involves one-on-one or small group coaching, using Coachbot analytics to pinpoint students requiring encouragement, accountability, or modified strategies. The final 10% is dedicated to examining data, refining coaching methods, and preparing students for greater success in the week ahead. You'll begin with established workshop frameworks, then enhance and expand them as you identify more effective ways to motivate students.

Performance metrics are clear. A minimum of 90% of your students should reliably achieve their weekly academic targets, demonstrate proficiency in Alpha's life skills via Test2Pass assessments, and provide ratings of at least 4 out of 5 for their experience with you. Maintain this standard consistently and you'll have a defined path to Lead Guide, mentoring other Guides, and ultimately Campus Lead, where you'll influence the culture and outcomes of an entire school.

This position isn't designed for those who prefer lecturing, adhering to fixed curricula, or simply occupying students. It's built for coaches, mentors, youth leaders, performers, tutors, and educators who define success by student transformation. Every finalist completes a full day coaching actual Alpha students before an offer is extended. If that prospect excites you more than another standard interview, we want to hear from you.

What You Will Be Doing

Facilitating high-energy, one-hour life skills workshops for K-8 students, building communication, resilience, focus, leadership, and other enduring skills while continuously refining the workshop delivery.
Providing individual and small group coaching using Coachbot analytics, customized accountability, and Alpha's motivational frameworks to support every student in reaching ambitious weekly objectives.
Evaluating life skill proficiency through Test2Pass and delivering focused coaching until each student displays authentic competence, not merely attendance.
Adjusting your coaching approach across elementary and middle school age groups, recognizing when a kindergartner requires movement and positive reinforcement and when an eighth grader benefits from direct accountability.
Reviewing weekly student performance metrics to detect patterns, eliminate barriers, and consistently enhance results across your entire cohort.

What You Won’t Be Doing

Providing traditional classroom instruction. AI manages academic content delivery so you can concentrate on student development.
Evaluating homework, developing lesson plans, or preparing students for standardized testing.
Supervising students while they work quietly on computers. Each day is dynamic, interactive, and coaching-focused.
Seeking permission before assisting a student in need. You possess the autonomy to respond promptly and take necessary action.
Handling parent communications or administrative documentation. Campus Leads maintain parent relationships so your attention stays on students.

Youth Development Specialist Key Responsibilities

Develop a cohort of students who reliably meet ambitious academic objectives, gain mastery of essential life skills, and cultivate the confidence, resilience, and ownership necessary to thrive long after their time at Alpha.

Basic Requirements

Willing to work in person at an Alpha campus in Malibu, CA; San Francisco, CA; Santa Barbara, CA; Boston, MA; New York City, NY; or Miami Beach, FL (relocation assistance provided)
Bachelor's degree in any discipline
At least 3 years of direct experience with K-8 students through teaching, coaching, tutoring, mentoring, camp leadership, or youth programs
Capable of providing a specific example of inspiring a student to accomplish a challenging goal, including your methods and the result
Enthusiastic about allowing AI to manage academic instruction while you concentrate on coaching, motivation, and life skills cultivation
Authorized to work in the United States without current or future visa sponsorship

Nice-to-have Requirements

Background coaching youth sports, debate, theater, camps, after-school programs, or other performance-oriented activities
Personal history of exceptional achievement in academics, athletics, leadership, or another competitive domain
Compelling stage presence and narrative ability that maintains student engagement without depending on volume or strict discipline
Proven success transforming disengaged, resistant, or struggling students into motivated, self-assured learners

About Alpha

Join the team building school around student growth

Alpha reimagines the school day around faster learning, stronger mentorship, and more time for students to build real-world skills.

Roles with real student impact:
Alpha hires teachers (guides), operators, admissions experts, school & curriculum leaders, and remote team members.

Education work that pays like it matters:
Alpha offers six-figure roles for people ready to help build a radically better school experience.

A culture built for builders:
Alpha is fast-moving, ambitious, and student focused. It’s for people who want to improve the system, not maintain it.

Alpha is where you can do the most meaningful work of your career.

There is so much to cover for this exciting role, and space here is limited. Hit the Apply button if you found this interesting and want to learn more. We look forward to meeting you!

Working with us

Harris County Resources for Children and Adults was founded in 1966 as the Harris County Child Welfare Board to provide support services for children taken under the wing of the Texas Department of Family and Protective Services. Under the supervision of the Director of The HAY Center Housing & Foundation Advancement, the Housing Campus Supervisor is responsible for overseeing the initial phase of the Housing Continuum (assessment, application and lease-up process), housing navigation services and supervision of case management services provided to The HAY Center Campus apartment residents. Ensures that staff achieves goals/objectives of the HAY Center's Campus Housing Program, fulfills all grant measures and outcomes, and follows all program policies/procedures which includes budget management.
Works closely with internal programs, the apartment management team, the Harris County Housing Authority and Harris County Housing and Community Development to ensure youth are receiving services as needed to remain stably housed.
Completes monthly, quarterly and yearly reporting to ensure compliance and deliverables are met.
Participates in HAY Center/Housing Continuum events as needed. Assists in planning Housing related workshops and activities

The Social Worker/Case Worker provides home-based, intensive, strength-based, comprehensive services using the Solution-Based Casework (SBC) framework.

Our Superstar Social Worker Candidate Is

Passionate about providing high quality services to families in child welfare
A lifetime learner, continuously developing their clinical skills
Dedicated to modeling strength-based, trauma-informed practice with families and colleagues.
Culturally humble with a commitment to the Good Shepherd Services mission, vision, and values

Major Duties Of Social Worker

Direct Work with Families

Provide home-based and on-site individual, family, and group counseling, as well as short-term crisis intervention, including advocacy and outreach for designated caseload of eight (8) families.
Engage families immediately upon referral, at times participating in Administration for Children’s Services (ACS) Child Safety Conferences.
Implement and integrate the principles and procedures of Solution-Based Casework (SBC): assessment, family and individual level outcomes, action plans, and documentation and celebration.
Handle case-related crises with professionalism, urgency, and care, including incidents involving reports to the State Central Registry.
Conduct screenings and assessments for substance use, mental illness, and child safety and well-being, including assessing caregiver capacity, home environment and conditions, discipline methods, etc.
Integrate the practices of SBC into every counseling session.
Ensure that every child has been seen and properly assessed every month.
Meet appropriate case work contacts for each phase of treatment: Initial, Baseline, and Stabilization.
Represent participant needs, concerns, and perspectives at all required ACS and GSS meetings and trainings.

Administrative and Advocacy Role

Collaborate closely with ACS, alcohol and other drug treatment providers, schools, medical and mental health clinics, and other resources serving family members.
Provide consultation to and collaborate with Family Workers as needed to ensure high quality services to families.
Collaborate with ACS Family Services Unit (FSU) staff, Family Court Legal Services (FCLS) staff and other service providers in making safety and treatment decisions.
Attend and participate in Family Court hearings for families involved with ACS FSU.
Facilitate referrals to alcohol and substance abuse treatment facilities, mental health treatment providers, and other service providers, including escorts to appointments as needed.
Actively participate in Clinical Diagnostic Team meetings (CDTs) to provide case information, updates, and assessments in order to obtain recommendations for continued case practice or case termination.
Participate in case consultation, continued SBC training, and the SBC certification process.
Prepare and maintain FASP documentation, monthly statistical reports, and case work notes in adherence with agency policy.
Provide Court reports as needed to inform as to families’ progress or lack of progress in achieving outcomes.
Maintain appropriate utilization of state and city databases including PROMIS and Connections, as well as other agency databases as needed.

Qualifications

Master's Degree Required (Must be relevant field Psychology; Social Work; Mental Health Counselling etc)
LMSW eligible candidates highly encouraged to apply! (We sponsor your exam-terms/conditions apply)
Child welfare experience preferred
Bilingual - English/Spanish Preferred
Must have strong organizational, interpersonal, and counseling skills
Must be able to work at least 2 evenings per week to accommodate working families’ schedules
Must have strong inquiry skills and ability to seek and share internal and external best practices
Must have a commitment to work from a strength based, trauma-informed & youth and family development perspective
SBC trained and/or SBC certified a plus
